title: Carrot and Coriander Soup
subtitle: A smooth, warmly spiced soup with a coconut swirl
excerpt: This soup blends to a vivid orange with a gentle warmth from cumin and ginger. A small amount of coconut milk stirred in at the end adds richness without heaviness. It freezes brilliantly.
sourceNotes: Carrot and coriander soup became one of the most popular homemade soups in Britain during the 1980s and 1990s as fresh coriander became more widely available in supermarkets.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze without the coconut milk swirl. Add it fresh when reheating. Keeps for 3 months.
recipe.batchNotes: Doubles well. Freeze in single-portion tubs.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Keeps refrigerated for 4 days. Reheat gently and thin with a splash of stock if needed.

content.text: Blending hot soup in a jug blender requires care. Fill the blender no more than halfway and hold the lid down firmly with a folded cloth.

items.prepNote: to swirl in at the end

content.text: Heat the oil in a large pot over a medium heat.
Add the onion and a pinch of salt. Cook for 8 minutes until soft.
Add the garlic and ginger. Cook for 2 minutes, stirring.
Add the spices. Stir and cook for 1 minute.
Add the carrots and stock. Bring to a boil, then reduce to a simmer.
Simmer for 20 to 25 minutes until the carrots are very tender.
Blend until completely smooth. Return to the pot.
Swirl a little coconut milk over each bowl. Scatter with coriander leaves.

items.symptom: Soup is too thick after blending.
items.cause: Carrots absorbed a lot of liquid during cooking.
items.fix: Stir in extra stock or hot water until the right consistency.

items.cause: Onion was not cooked long enough before adding the carrots.
items.fix: Cook onion until it is soft and lightly golden before moving on.

items.cause: Blender too full with hot liquid.
items.fix: Fill halfway, hold lid down with a cloth, blend in short bursts.
